findings.problem: The canonical rewrite `endpointSpatialMap = chart (N+L) (endpointTopCell ..)` is not a simp lemma. Neither is the unfolding of `RefinedAffineMap.vertex` to `chart hp N q (FiniteSimplex.vertex i)`. Every user has to pass both as ad-hoc simp arguments. The same pair is copied into both `lower_value_eq` and `upper_value_eq`, and the same simp-set pattern appears in other files (RelativeCollarMiddlePrismEndpointsCore, EquivariantPrismStableRelativeBoundary). Because `vertex` is unfolded by name, any change to its definition breaks all of those call sites.
findings.proposed_change: In EndpointFaceRefinement, consider marking `endpointSpatialMap_eq_chart` as `@[simp]`. It rewrites toward the ordinary chart at level `N+L`, which looks like the intended normal form. Alongside it, add a `RefinedAffineMap.vertex_def` or `vertex_eq_chart_vertex` equation lemma and use that instead of unfolding. Then both `simpa` calls could become `simpa using hsample`, or a single shared lemma could serve the lower and upper cases. Before doing this, check that no existing `endpointSpatialMap` simp lemmas conflict with the new rule.
findings.benefit: Call sites no longer need to list the lemma and unfold `vertex` by name. The lower and upper proofs stop being copies that must be kept in sync. The simp normal form for endpoint spatial maps becomes the chart at the combined level, which matches the level-equality statements this file proves.
